articles.title: Brendan Venter: Saracens media duties 'like something from an autocratic land'
articles.summary: Saracens' Brendan Venter compares Prem Rugby's media obligations to "something from an autocratic land" after reluctantly speaking at a press conference.
articles.body:
Saracens' Brendan Venter compared Prem Rugby's media obligations to "something from an autocratic land" after he made a reluctant appearance at a press conference.

The 56-year-old returned to a full-time role at the club in the summer, initially as director of rugby, but has since been given an updated job title of head of culture and technical director.

His no-show at a pre-season media event cost Saracens a £5,000 fine and he avoided questions before and after the club's opening-round win over Leicester.

However, he appeared alongside head coach Joe Shaw to preview this Saturday's match against Bristol and, after initially offering only short answers to reporters' questions, railed against the expectation that he would be the public face of the club.

"I have the desire as a human being not to want to talk," he said. "It is not about me, it is about the team… I expressed that desire before I came."

Venter added: "I asked really kindly and eventually I bent over backwards to explain my position. And then I'm expected again to come and do an interview.

"If we get obsessed, get into an argument and fine a club, that for me does not make sense.

"It sounds like something from an autocratic land, not a democracy where people have the right to say: 'This is what I want to do'.

"If you want an interview, you have a brilliant person in Joe. I do not have the desire to do an interview. It stole my joy the previous time and I want to have a low profile.

"That was my desire and to help to coach the rugby team. I do not want to be doing interviews. It's not because I think I'm better than anybody else. To be put over as an arrogant person who thinks he's better than doing interviews… it's not at all that."

Venter's previous 16-month spell in charge of Saracens was littered with controversy.

He also ignored the obligation for club captain Steve Borthwick to attend a Heineken Cup launch event, instead sending the now England coach on a beer-fuelled team-bonding trip to Munich.

After one reprimand by European rugby authorities, Venter gave a viral post-match interview, inspired by a scene from the film Mike Bassett: England Manager, , external in which he agreed with the premise of every question asked of him.

After leaving Saracens in 2011, Venter, who won the Rugby World Cup as a player with South Africa in 1995, worked in roles with Durban-based club side the Sharks, as well as with Italy and South Africa.

The changes to his job title since his return to north London, which reportedly included a stint as the club's wine consultant that lasted a matter of days, , external appeared to be an attempt to escape his media obligations.

Prem Rugby rules require the most senior coach in every club to carry out routine media duties.

Their job titles can vary. Rob Baxter is Exeter's director of rugby. George Skivington is Gloucester's head coach. But as the principle decision-maker for their team, both answer questions each week.

Venter claimed in a weekend interview with TNT Sport, the broadcaster who pays £40m a season for action and access to the Prem, that decisions over team selection are done on the basis of a consensus, rather than any single person having a final say.

Regardless, it is expected the Venter will continue to face the media for the rest of the campaign.

Venter added that, despite his reservations, he had been tempted back by a love of coaching and the high-intensity dressing room environment.

"I love coaching rugby. I love working with players. It is a privilege we get as human beings to be in a position where we can influence things, both good and bad," he added.

"People in life rarely get that privilege.

"It's a phenomenal game to be a part of and that's why when [Saracens owner] Dominic [Silvester] asked me, I agreed to come back.

"You make friends like you never make in your life. When there are good times and difficult times, it builds character. I'm privileged enough to be doing that on a daily basis."

Venter did not win any silverware during his first stint in charge of Saracens. His side lost to Leicester in the 2010 Premiership final, a match Venter was banned from as part of a touchline suspension.

However, he left behind a formidably talented and closely bonded squad who would win multiple domestic and European honours under McCall in the following decade.

In behind-the-scenes footage of Venter's speech to his squad at the start of pre-season, he set out his ambition to contend for the Prem title.

"I promise you I don't want to be competitive in this league. I want to dominate," he said.

"This is not a team with a ceiling, this is something special, I have not come all this way to be average."

articles.title: Shanelle Williams: Wales hooker realises childhood dream and prepares for Japan
articles.summary: Shanelle Williams has realised a childhood dream of playing for Wales and now the hooker wants more caps, beginning with two Tests against Japan in WXV.
articles.body:
Shanelle Williams has already fulfilled one childhood ambition after making her Wales debut and now she is preparing for another milestone in Japan.

The 19-year-old former Gwernyfed RFC junior came off the bench in Wales' 50-19 win over South Africa in the WXV Global Series in September.

As a child, Williams had written on her Christmas list that she wanted to play for Wales.

"I didn't actually know that there was a women's team," the hooker said.

"I used to tell my dad that I was going to play for Wales with the boys.

"Then I obviously realised that I actually can play for Wales. Since then, everything I've done, rugby's always been a priority."

Williams had forgotten about the Christmas list until her older sister reminded her after she won her first Wales Under-18 cap.

"It's quite a nice reminder that I have been working for this for so long, so it has all been worth it," she said.

Williams started playing rugby at Gwernyfed aged eight, spending four years there before joining the Red Kites and later moving into the Wales pathway.

She went on to play for Cardiff Quins and Cardiff Rugby before attending Hartpury College.

Her father played a key role, regularly making the journey from home to Cardiff for training.

"Obviously I'm from Gwernyfed, so it was about an hour and a half down to Cardiff," she said.

"He used to take me for training on Friday nights straight after school.

"I wouldn't have been able to do it if my dad hadn't given me that opportunity, so I'm very lucky."

Williams' family and friends were in the stands to watch her make her Wales debut at Cardiff Arms Park.

"They'll come to every single game that they can," she said.

"It's so nice to be able to have that support on the sideline. I can always hear them over everyone else in the crowd."

Williams says the reality of becoming a senior Wales international only really sank in once she stepped onto the pitch.

"It didn't feel real it until I was actually on the pitch," she said.

"It was quite nice to be able to come onto the pitch with Elan (Jones) as well, because we've done [Wales] Under-18s together, we've done Under-20s together.

"Being able to share that with her was really nice as well. Then coming to my family afterwards, it was a surreal feeling, to be honest."

The Brython Thunder hooker has been inclued in a 30-player squad for two Tests against Japan which will complete Wales' WXV Global Series campaign for 2026.

The first Test takes place at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium in Tokyo on Saturday, 24 October at 10:30 BST, with the second at Kumagaya Rugby Stadium in Saitama seven days later at 07:00 GMT.

Williams admits the senior international environment has been a significant step up.

"I'd heard a lot from my friends - 'It is a step up, it is a step up'," she said.

"I think that actually prepared me quite well to understand that it's not just going into another pathway camp.

"There's even more competition and also understanding that there are still people behind you chasing for your position as well. I think that pushes you a lot more.

"So yeah, it's definitely been a step up, but I've been enjoying it."

Metcalfe back in Wales WXV reckoning for Japan

Lynn remaining positive despite Wales' USA setback

Lions tour a 'top goal' for Wales prop Tuipulotu

'It's the longest flight I've ever been on'

Japan will also provide Williams with a new experience off the pitch.

"It's the longest flight I've ever been on," she said.

"I've only ever been to Italy, I think that's the furthest I've been - two hours. So I'm not sure how that's going to go."

But she is determined to make the most of her opportunity against a Japan side ranked 12th in the world, one place below Wales.

"Sometimes, because they're not in the Six Nations and stuff, they can be a little bit overlooked," she said.

"They are a good team, so it's just making sure we stay on top of our process.

"We've done a lot over pre-season on being an 80-minute team, so I think sticking to that should help us."

Williams has already achieved the dream she wrote down as a child. Now she wants to add to her Wales cap tally.

"I've always looked up to girls like Kelsey Jones, Molly Reardon and Carys Phillips when she was in the squad," she said.

"They've always been role models to me, so being able to train alongside them and get tips from them as well is really beneficial to me.

"Definitely, I want to add to that tally."

articles.title: Jason Gilmore: Harlequins head coach anticipated difficult start to Prem season
articles.summary: Harlequins head coach Jason Gilmore says he expected a difficult start to the season following a summer of changes.
articles.body:
Harlequins head coach Jason Gilmore says he expected a difficult start to the season following a summer of changes.

Quins are bottom of the Prem table after losing their first two matches.

They produced a woeful performance in Saturday's 48-0 thrashing by Gloucester - the club's heaviest league defeat for 26 years.

"We're certainly not going to be at our best early doors, but it won't be too far away," Gilmore told BBC Radio London.

"There will be bumps here and there, but the weekend wasn't one we can accept. We've just got to stick to task."

Having been in interim charge for six months after Danny Wilson left Harlequins to join Wales' coaching team, Gilmore was confirmed as permanent boss in March.

That was despite a miserable season in which Quins ended the campaign ninth in the table - their lowest finish for eight years.

Robbie Deans was brought in as performance director and there were further changes, with Rob Hunter, formerly of Exeter Chiefs, coming in as forwards coach and Brad Cooper arriving as attack coach.

Gloucester thrash sorry Quins to go top of the Prem

Quins display one of worst I have ever seen - Monye

Gilmore declared last month he had "no doubt" his side would perform better this time around, after a "new start" for the club.

But their performances so far suggest there is plenty of work to do.

He described the debacle against Gloucester as "unacceptable", but says a bumpy start was always likely.

"We've been learning a brand new attack system and we've got a brand new line-out system that we're putting in place that's going to take four to six weeks just to bed down," he added.

"We've got the international players that have just come back into the building as well that are learning it on the run.

"They've done their prep work, but there are two massive pieces of your game that we're still building and still learning."

Former Harlequins and England winger Ugo Monye called the abject display against Gloucester "one of the worst performances" he has ever seen.

"They got smashed in the scrum and line-out, their backfield coverage was poor, they got smashed at the gain line," Monye said on the Rugby Union Weekly podcast .

"They didn't score a single point in a league where they're literally handing out points for free."

And Gilmore has made his feelings clear to his squad.

He explained: "It's not 'going at' the players, it's more just being honest about things that we wanted to do that we didn't do.

"What we don't want to do is jump at shadows. We've had a pretty reasonable four weeks leading into that, so we've just got to get back on the tools and work as hard as we can and put out a good performance this weekend."

This Sunday, Harlequins are away to Sale, who claimed their first win of the season by beating Saracens last weekend despite having Jacques Vermeulen sent off.

"That's the beauty of sport - now you get your chance to redeem yourself," said Gilmore.

"If we could have played the game a bit sooner after the Gloucester game to get back out there, you'd definitely choose that.

"We're working hard this week in our prep, as the boys always do, and we're keen to go up there and show the best versions of ourselves."

articles.title: Super League: Wakefield top rankings as all 14 Super League clubs stay for 2027
articles.summary: The 14 Super League clubs will remain in place for 2027 with Grand Final winners Wakefield Trinity topping the IMG ratings.
articles.body:
All 14 Super League clubs will remain in the competition next season after the release of the yearly gradings, with Wakefield Trinity topping the ratings for the first time.

Following their Super League Grand Final success, Wakefield have come top of the ratings, based on criteria formulated by media giant IMG, with marks for five factors - fan experience, finance, stadium, community and on-field performance.

London Broncos have come 16th on the list, below fellow Championship side Barrow Raiders, despite a season in which they won the second tier's Grand Final, the 1895 Cup and were runaway champions in the regular-season standings.

The Broncos were overlooked 12 months ago when Bradford Bulls, York Knights and Toulouse Olympique joined the expanded 14-team competition.

But, with the backing of Australian businessman Grant Wechsel, former Brisbane Broncos star Darren Lockyer and a squad full of internationals, they do still harbour hopes of playing in Super League in 2027.

Australia's National Rugby League (NRL) is looking to invest in the competition, with talks at an advanced stage.

It is understood any completed deal would involve the Australian governing body insisting on Broncos featuring in the top flight next season.

London Broncos rout Doncaster to clinch treble

What are IMG gradings and how do they work?

Wakefield have matched 2025 champions Hull KR's record grading score of 17.85 from 12 months ago, to continue their rise on and off the field under Matt Ellis' ownership. In the same rankings last year they were eighth with a mark of 15.47, only just above the threshold for Category A status.

"Wakefield Trinity's rise to the top of the 2026 club grading rankings is a fascinating story for rugby league, and a strong example of how sustained progress on and off the field can be recognised through the grading framework," said RFL chief executive Ian Nolan.

"Their achievement sits alongside encouraging movement across the sport, from growing attendances and digital audiences to continued improvements in facilities and community delivery."

Leeds Rhinos remain second, although their score of 17.03 is slightly lower than they achieved in the 2025 rankings.

Warrington Wolves have jumped from sixth to third on the back of a much stronger season which culminated in reaching the Grand Final at Old Trafford, only to lose to Wakefield.

It is fourth place again for Wigan, who won both the Challenge Cup and the League Leaders' shield, just above Hull KR and Leigh Leopards. St Helens drop from third to seventh after a season in which they missed out on the play-offs for the first time in the Super League era.

Castleford Tigers complete the Category A clubs as they have risen from 11th in 2025 to eighth and move into the top-tier section despite finishing 13th in Super League.

Catalans Dragons and Hull FC are ninth and 10th, but both have fallen from an A to a B grade. Then come Bradford Bulls and Huddersfield Giants, with Toulouse Olympique and York Knights, occupying 13th and 14th, albeit with higher scores than last year.

However, only six of the 14 Super League clubs have scored higher than they did 12 months ago.

But there was a significant gap to the teams outside. York's score of 13.24 was comfortably higher than the next best, Barrow with 9.85, while London only achieved 9.77, which was down on their mark of 11.65 from last year.

Overall, 26 clubs were graded on this system, , external split into three categories, A, B and C.

articles.title: New Zealand vs Australia: All Blacks and Wallabies gear up for Bledisloe Cup Test with history for both at stake at Eden Park on Sky Sports
articles.summary: Watch New Zealand vs Australia in Bledisloe Cup Test on Saturday, live on Sky Sports Main Event from 7am; Wallabies unbeaten in six Tests, while All Blacks seeking to avoid four successive Test losses for first time since 1998; New Zealand have held Bledisloe since 2002
articles.body:
Not only that, they face an All Blacks side suffering from injuries and under pressure to avoid a fourth Test defeat in a row for the first time in some 28 years, dating back to 1998.

Under new head coach Les Kiss, the Wallabies have beaten Japan home and away, beaten Argentina at home and drawn against them away, and beaten South Africa in Perth despite finishing with just 11 players in a madcap Test match.

That run of games was preceded by victory over Italy in July, meaning Australia are on a six-Test unbeaten run for the first time since 2017.

Yet to continue such a run, Australia are going to have to create several massive pieces of history.

Firstly, they face the All Blacks at Eden Park on Saturday, where the men in black have not suffered defeat since July 1994 against France. A remarkable 32-year record, stretching 51 unbeaten Tests (49 wins, two draws).

Of course, New Zealand travel around the country to play their Test matches rather than having one permanent home, so the record is unique in that sense, but over the three decades since that last defeat in Auckland, New Zealand have lost 15 home Tests, but none at Eden Park.

Secondly, New Zealand are on a record win streak of 11 Tests in a row against Australia since the Wallabies last tasted success in November 2020 during COVID times, and have held the Bledisloe Cup for the last 24 years.

Indeed, Australia held the Bledisloe between 1998 and 2002, and have never held it since.

To hold the Bledisloe Cup, you have to win more contests between the sides in a year than the other, with any years drawn seeing the current holders retain it. The record has been drawn in five calendar years for New Zealand to retain, while they have also won out in 18 of the years since.

This New Zealand had shown an uptick under Dave Rennie, winning his opening four Tests, including beating the Springboks in South Africa with a stunning 33-16 success at Ellis Park, but have since had the stuffing knocked out of them with three straight Test defeats to the Boks in Cape Town, Johannesburg and Baltimore, USA.

Therefore, for New Zealand to lose on Saturday, they would have to suffer defeat in a Test for the fourth time in a row. The last time that happened? 1998, in the midst of a five-match losing run to Australia (three times) and South Africa (twice).

In 181 previous Tests between New Zealand and Australia dating back to 1903, there have been 128 All Blacks wins to 45 wins for the Wallabies, with eight draws.

In 123 years of history between the nations, Australia have only won in New Zealand on 15 occasions. The weight of history is firmly against them.

Kiss: We're going to have to be very good | Rennie: We have a point to prove

Australia have exuded a quiet confidence since ‌Kiss took over as coach in late July.

The All Blacks will be without totemic forward Ardie Savea as well as playmakers Ruben Love and Richie Mo'unga because of injury, but Kiss was still awed ​by the quality of the team his counterpart Rennie was able to name on Thursday.

"I know ⁠they've had a few injuries, but strewth, when you look at ⁠that team, it makes it tough," Kiss told reporters after naming his side on Thursday.

"We're going to have to be good, that's for sure, to go out there and ‌put something on that can compete."

The All Blacks are coming off four bruising Tests against the Springboks, determined to end the streak of losses which cost them that series.

"No one wants to be part of the first team for a long time to lose at Eden Park, or lose the Bledisloe," Rennie said.

"We've come out of South Africa. We've got a bit of a point to prove there and we're ⁠up against really worthy opponents, and we know we're going to have to be at our ​best."

Rennie knows many of the Australia team well, having coached the Wallabies from 2020 ​until he was summarily sacked in early 2023 to make way for the ill-fated return of Eddie Jones.

The ​62-year-old, however, was quick to quash any suggestion that his brutal sacking would add to his team's motivation.

"It's ⁠not about me," he said. "I've got no regrets. I got to work with some really good people, people I have a lot of time for, and it's a part of a game that we're involved in."

For the Wallabies, a win on Saturday to earn a ⁠shot at winning back the Bledisloe Cup in next week's second ​Test in Sydney would be transformational to their profile in Australia less than a year out from a ​Rugby World Cup on home soil.

Kiss, though, was wary of leaving any hostages to fortune when asked if the Wallabies could finally end the Eden Park hoodoo.

"I think this is a team that ‌can step forward and see how close we ​can take it," he said.

McKenzie at fly-half for All Blacks as Barrett returns | Australia's Henry in for Paisami

Damian McKenzie will start at fly-half with veteran Beauden Barrett at full-back as a spate of injuries has shaped the All Blacks line-up to face Australia.

Love has already been ruled out for the season with an ankle injury, while Mo'unga injured a calf muscle at training on Tuesday, leaving McKenzie and Barrett - both preferred as full-backs - to share the playmaker roles in the wake of New Zealand's 3-1 series loss to world champions South Africa.

"Damian's trained a lot [at fly-half] for us. Beauden's predominantly trained at 15 when we're in Africa," Rennie said. "I think both those players are interchangeable. They both spend a lot of time in the backfield. The way we play, having a 15 who is a real playmaker suits.

"We could have played them the other way around but they'll both end up in playmaker roles and they'll both end up in the backfield."

With Caleb Clarke unavailable with a shoulder injury and Fehi Fineanganofo sidelined with concussion, Will Jordan and Leroy Carter will start on the wings. Jordie Barrett and Quinn Tupaea combine in midfield in the absence of Billy Proctor and Anton Lienert-Brown, who also have injuries.

The back-row is unchanged, with captain Savea out of action for several months due to shoulder surgery.

Former captain Scott Barrett will make his first Test appearance of the season, returning at lock, as the three Barrett brothers start together for the first time this year. Hooker Codie Taylor retains the captaincy.

For Australia, Isaac Henry will start at centre in place of Hunter Paisami, who is suspended, in the only change to the Wallabies starting line-up. Henry will combine in midfield with Len Ikitau.

Among a number of changes on a 5-3 bench, prop Massimo De Lutiis replaces Taniela Tupou, who has rejoined his French club. Lachlan Shaw will make his first Bledisloe Cup appearance as a replacement alongside Nick Champion de Crespigny, who is named on the bench for only his second match of the year.

"Keeping consistency in the starting side gives us a solid foundation, while adding some freshness on the bench will provide energy late in the game," Kiss said.

"There aren't many tougher challenges than playing New Zealand at Eden Park, but it's one we're excited by and know that we will need to be at our best in all aspects of our game."

articles.title: Taulupe Faletau: Wales forward back from injury for Cardiff at Leinster in URC
articles.summary: Wales number eight Taulupe Faletau is set to make his first appearance since March in the United Rugby Championship on Saturday.
articles.body:
Wales number eight Taulupe Faletau will make his first appearance since March when starting for Cardiff at Leinster in the United Rugby Championship (URC).

The 35-year-old has not played since suffering a shoulder injury at Sharks, a blow that ended an injury-hit campaign that also featured knee and calf problems.

Faletau will make his return as Cardiff, fresh from wins against Scarlets and Zebre, make seven changes for the trip to the redeveloped Laya Arena in Dublin on Saturday (19:45 BST).

Captain Liam Belcher returns at hooker and full-back Matty Young, who scored at Stade Francais in the Challenge Cup last season, makes his URC debut.

There are also starts for wing Mason Grady, scrum-half Aled Davies, loose-head prop Danny Southworth and open-side flanker Dan Thomas.

Wales back row Faletau signs new Cardiff deal

Inside Scarlets and their struggle for existence

Tonga lock or back-row forward Semisi Paea is poised for a Cardiff debut off the bench.

The Blue and Blacks face a Leinster side who claimed three bonus points when starting the defence of their title in South Africa against Lions and Sharks.

Cardiff head coach Corniel van Zyl said: "We are really excited to travel to Ireland for what will be a big test against the URC champions.

"It's been a pleasing start to the season for us in terms of results but there is plenty to work on in terms of performance and we want to take another step forward this week."

Leinster head coach Leo Cullen names an entirely new starting line-up from the bonus-point defeat by Sharks in Durban, bringing back a host of Ireland internationals.

Hooker and captain Dan Sheehan, tight-head prop Tadgh Furlong, locks Joe McCarthy and James Ryan, number eight Jack Conan, centre Garry Ringrose and full-back Hugo Keenan all play for the first time since starting against New Zealand in the Nations Championship.

Fly-half Sam Prendergast, who pulled the strings against the All Blacks, starts after coming off the bench at Sharks.

The Irish province are playing their first competitive fixture at Laya Arena, formerly known as the Royal Dublin Society, since 2024 after playing for two seasons at Aviva Stadium while redevelopment work was carried out.

articles.title: Charlie Atkinson: Gloucester fly-half on Kingsholm resurgence
articles.summary: Charlie Atkinson has had three professional clubs and plenty of set-backs in his career so far, but now he is riding high with a resurgent Gloucester
articles.body:
Charlie Atkinson can see the funny side now.

"I mean, I met my hero," he says smilingly.

Atkinson is remembering his second Prem appearance, back in September 2020. He was 18 years old. He had been ushered straight into the Wasps first team as squads were stretched to fulfil a condensed post-lockdown fixture list

Atkinson had just come off the bench against Saracens when, having fielded a kick downfield, he was blindsided by Owen Farrell's reckless, high tackle. Atkinson was left unconscious on the Stonex pitch as the referee showed red.

Farrell was instantly contrite, waiting on the touchline to check on Atkinson and then visiting him again in the dressing room.

The incident, as with anything involving Farrell, attracted attention and debate.

"It definitely put my name out there," adds Atkinson.

"It was obviously accidental, but as it was a concussion I was sent home for the week, I didn't play again that season. It was probably a good thing, slowing down so that at 18, I could just focus on training and getting used to men's rugby."

Atkinson is good at seeing the upside. He has had to be. Perspective comes with experience and he has been through plenty already in his rugby career.

Three days after his 21st birthday, having established himself as his boyhood club's first-choice fly-half, he unknowingly played in Wasps' final ever game, a dramatic 40-36 defeat by Northampton.

"We'd seen a few rumours on Twitter that week but nothing major and we hadn't heard anything from the owner or CEO, so we just thought 'we'll be alright'," he says.

"It was a wasn't even really in the back of my mind.

"That next Tuesday or Wednesday they broke the news that our jobs were gone. It was obviously very sad, it was the only club I ever knew."

After Wasps went into administration in October 2022, Gloucester and Harlequins made approaches to sign Atkinson. But he was convinced by a meeting with Steve Borthwick, who had just steered Leicester to the Premiership title and was offering the security of a longer deal.

Atkinson duly signed up with Tigers. Borthwick and assistant Kevin Sinfield departed for England two months later.

Under new boss Dan McKellar, Atkinson endured a difficult year at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, shunted to the fringes.

Still, he had just completed on a house purchase in Leicester, when, a week later, his agent informed him Gloucester had agreed a deal to take him to Kingsholm.

Finally, despite the upheaval, he has found a home.

"I'm just forever grateful for Gloucester for coming in then because who knows where I could have ended up if I'd stayed at the Tigers," he says.

"I love coming in here every day. There is a great, young core of guys, we made some great signings in the summer and everyone's mates with everyone. It's just a great feeling at the minute."

Gloucester, who finished eighth last season, have started this campaign like a train.

Buoyed by the arrival of Jac Morgan, Dewi Lake, Jean Kleyn and others, they combined heft up front with deft hands out back to beat Prem finalist Exeter on the opening day, before flattening Harlequins 48-0 in front of a bouncing home crowd.

The Cherry and Whites sit in an unaccustomed position on the top of the Prem pile.

Up next, on Friday night, is a return to Leicester for Atkinson.

After the match, he will meet up with Jack van Poortvliet, Freddie Steward and others who he became mates with during his time at Tigers.

Such is Atkinson's form, he could be spending more time with them in England camps.

Atkinson's solitary cap came in July 2025, coming on for the final 18 minutes of a 40-5 win over the United States.

He has been a regular for England A since and on the edge of a senior squad overseen by Borthwick, the man who signed him at Leicester.

"There are three main 10s at the minute in Fin Smith, George Ford and Marcus Smith, so it a very good level of competition," said Atkinson.

"I'm just focusing on how much I can help Gloucester and how consistent and effective my performances can be.

"But obviously that's always going to be in the back of my mind, how I can get another cap or get back into a camp. But right now, it's all about continuing this momentum.

"There's a lot more for me to give here at Gloucester and right now is probably the best rugby that I've ever played."

Atkinson has played more at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium as a mini rugby player than a professional one.

Twice as a youngster, he turned out for Oxford RFC as part of the half-time entertainment in the Premiership's London double header fixtures.

Gloucester's last play-off visit to the venue was similarly long ago – a 44-16 defeat by Friday's opponents Leicester in the 2007 Premiership final.

Whether with club or country, Atkinson may be due a return soon.

articles.title: Sale v Harlequins: Joe Carpenter eyes duel with George Furbank and England return
articles.summary: In-form Sale full-back Joe Carpenter admits part of him is focused on outshining Harlequins' George Furbank this weekend to advance his case for an England recall.
articles.body:
In-form Sale full-back Joe Carpenter admits part of him is focused on outshining Harlequins' George Furbank this weekend in an attempt to force his way back into the England reckoning.

Only Exeter wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso has beaten more defenders in the first two rounds of the Prem this season, as Carpenter has shown a keen attacking edge.

Furbank was England's first-choice full-back this summer before an appendicitis sidelined him for last summer's Nations Championship, while Carpenter has not been involved in Steve Borthwick's set-up since winning his only Test cap in a 40-5 win over the United States in July 2025.

Their two sides meet at Sale's Corpacq Stadium on Sunday, with Quins looking for their first points of a miserable campaign so far.

"Yeah I'd say so, in a certain aspect," said Carpenter when asked if the personal duel with Furbank was motivation.

"Those boys [Harlequins] have just come off the back of a pretty big loss and they'll be emotionally spiked come this weekend.

"So yeah it would be nice to have a very good performance against them and against that England competition"

Carpenter, who also scored a hat-trick of tries against Bath in the Prem Cup last month, partly puts his fast start to the season down to missing out on England selection.

After touring Japan and New Zealand in 2024 and Argentina and the United States in 2025, Carpenter's absence from a gruelling long-haul Nations Championship trip enabled him to take part in a full club pre-season for the first time in three years.

"Those summer tours are very intense - training's competitive, the games even more so - so to miss out on that was unfortunate," Carpenter added.

"But to actually get a full 10 weeks of pre-season and preparation, getting the body right, was definitely something I needed. I think it's shown in spades really from the games, I feel a lot fitter and a lot stronger.

"I'm just probably outside the mix [for England] at the moment but having back-to-back performances and playing as well as possible will definitely put me in the best position to hopefully get involved come November."

England coaches have challenged Carpenter to improve his decision-making in backfield and his stamina to cover ground and repeatedly take on tacklers. He scored highly in Sale's fitness testing when he reported for pre-season and has been an elusive threat with ball in hand.

"Beating defenders is a massive part of my game," he added.

"But that repeatability is massive and something that I'm definitely feeling the benefits of, being able to go again and again and again at speed.

"It is putting me in better positions and giving me more opportunities to not only just get the ball, but affect the play positively when I do."

Carpenter admitted that, after reaching the play-offs in each of his previous three seasons at the club, a disappointing seventh-place finish in Sale's last campaign gave him pause for thought before he signed a new deal with the club this summer.

Sale won only five of their 18 league matches in the league and were on the wrong end of an 85-19 drubbing by Saracens in April. They were also comfortably beaten by Leinster in the last eight of the Champions Cup.

However, coach Alex Sanderson has been backed, with former England captain Courtney Lawes heading a clutch of new signings.

Lawes, backed up by the experienced Tom Curry and George Ford, produced a fine performance as Sharks claimed only their second-ever league win away to Saracens last weekend.

"After last season, re-signing was probably a bit tougher than it could potentially be," said Carpenter.

"But after speaking to the coaches, understanding the game model going forward and hearing the signings that are coming in, I think it would have been very silly to leave."

articles.title: Shaun Edwards: Coveted defence coach signs contract with Argentina until after 2027 Rugby World Cup
articles.summary: Former Wales and France defence coach Shaun Edwards - currently working with Red Roses on short-term basis - signs on with Argentina until end of 2027 Rugby World Cup; Watch New Zealand vs Australia in Bledisloe Cup Test on Saturday, live on Sky Sports Main Event from 7am
articles.body:
Edwards is currently working with England's Red Roses under John Mitchell until after the conclusion of the WXV Global Series on October 30.

As such, the 59-year-old will work with the Pumas through their Nations Championship Tests in Europe this November and throughout 2027 until the conclusion of the World Cup.

Edwards was sacked as France's defence coach earlier this year, having worked as part of their Six Nations title successes in 2022 (Grand Slam), 2025 and 2026.

Edwards also worked alongside Warren Gatland in the Wales setup between 2008 and 2019, winning Six Nations titles in 2008, 2012, 2013 and 2019.

The former Wigan Warriors rugby league great also worked as British and Irish Lions defence coach on the 2009 tour of South Africa.

Joining Argentina will only be the fifth role of Edwards' standout 25-year coaching career, with the Pumas joining the Red Roses, Wasps, Wales and France on his CV.

The former Great Britain captain was unexpectedly axed in the wake of France's Six Nations title triumph in March, having been in charge of their defence since 2020. Head coach Fabien Galthie revealed in June he wanted to shake-up a back-room team that had been place in long-term.

Signing a contract with Argentina ends any chance of Edwards joining the England men's coaching team under Borthwick.

News of Edwards joining Argentina was confirmed alongside news Mario Ledesma will return as Pumas forwards coach, having worked as head coach between 2018 and 2022.

Argentina head coach Felipe Contepomi said: "Mario and Shaun arrive at Los Pumas with enormous international experience. They know what it means to compete at the highest level and can contribute a lot to the team.

"With the World Cup just a year away, they will help us continue to grow as a team and prepare in the best possible way for what's to come."

Edwards said: "I'm thrilled to be joining Felipe Contepomi, his coaching staff, and the Argentinian team at the end of this month and through to next year's World Cup in Australia.

"I've always admired the skill and quality of Argentinian players, and I look forward to contributing my international experience to the team over the next year."

Ledesma commented: " I am honored and very grateful for the opportunity to work with Los Pumas again. I am eager for us to get together and start working with the players and the staff."

articles.title: Shaun Edwards takes Argentina defence coach role
articles.summary: Defence coach Shaun Edwards joins Argentina's coaching staff on a deal that runs until the end of the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia.
articles.body:
Defence coach Shaun Edwards has joined Argentina's coaching staff on a deal that runs until the end of the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia.

The announcement ends any speculation that Edwards could be handed a role in Steve Borthwick's England set-up, with the 59-year-old set to fulfil his consultancy role with England's women's team before joining Felipe Contepomi's staff.

"I'm delighted to join Felipe Contepomi, his coaching staff and the Argentina rugby team at the end of this month until the World Cup next year in Australia," said Edwards.

"I've always admired the ability and quality of Argentine players and I hope to bring some of my international experience to the team during the next year," added the former Wigan rugby league great.

Englishman Edwards, who is one of the most decorated coaches in rugby union, left his position as France men's defence coach earlier this year after helping them win three Six Nations titles.

Edwards and former Argentina head coach and hooker Mario Ledesma, who has been appointed to take charge of the forwards, will start work with the Pumas at the end of October.

Argentina are then set to face Ireland, Italy and France in November in Nations Championship matches.

Three-time semi-finalists Argentina have been drawn in a pool with Fiji, Spain and Canada at the World Cup which takes place between 1 October and 13 November in 2027.

Edwards, who also spent a successful 12 years with Wales and won four English titles and two Champions Cups while on Wasps' staff, said in March that he was interested in coaching in the Rugby Championship, the southern hemisphere tournament contested by South Africa, New Zealand, Australia and Argentina.

He turned down a chance to coach his country in 2006, believing that the busier fixture list at Wasps would suit him better as he grieved the death of his brother.

Two years later, he opted to take on a defence role with Wales, rather than lead England's second-string side, then known as the Saxons. , external

In 2021, he met with Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney but, without a firm offer forthcoming, signed a contract extension to stay with France.

articles.title: Leicester 38-31 Gloucester: Tigers battle back to earn first home win of season
articles.summary: Leicester Tigers recover from a disastrous start to battle back and beat Gloucester for their first home win of the season.
articles.body:
Tries: Carnduff, Heyes, Blamire, Wainwright, Hassell-Collins Cons: Searle 5 Pens: Searle.

Tries: Morgan, Bleuler, Trenholm, Innard Cons: Englefield 2, Barton 2 Pens: Barton

Leicester Tigers recovered from a disastrous start to battle back and beat Gloucester for their first home win of the season.

Jac Morgan and Dian Bleuler both touched down for the Cherry and Whites when Tigers had Billy Searle in the sin-bin early on, but the hosts hit back with tries from Finn Carnduff, Joe Heyes and Jamie Blamire to lead 21-14 at the break.

Aaron Wainwright and Ollie Hassell-Collins scores either side of a Will Trenholm try for Gloucester proved enough to earn Tigers a hard-earned win.

And while beaten for the first time this season, Gloucester ensured they remain top of the Prem after earning two late bonus points after Jack Innard went over and George Barton landed an 82nd-minute penalty in a game watched by the Duke of Sussex.

Prince Harry's attendance added to sense of occasion at Mattioli Woods Welford Road as Leicester kept their hands on the Slater Cup – a trophy that honours former Gloucester and Tigers captain Ed Slater, who retired in 2022 after being diagnosed with Motor Neurone Disease (MND).

Searle's sin-binning in the second minute for a deliberate knock-on proved to be a costly one in a chaotic early showing by the hosts.

And while referee Karl Dickson denied Gloucester a penalty try - insisting Tigers had the numbers back to cover the danger - the Cherry and Whites were quick to burrow over for the game's first try through Morgan.

Another penalty, line-out and drive had Bleuler powering over for the visitors again soon after, but once they were back at full strength, Tigers hastily grabbed a carbon copy try in response as Carnduff ploughed over.

A clever cross-field kick from Searle that was collected by Freddie Steward helped set Tigers up for their second try of the night, which Heyes did well to finish from close range, while another catch and drive effort had Blamire touchdown to put Tigers ahead for the first time.

Tigers' fierce defensive showing early in the second half eventually earned Searle a penalty to extend that lead, while the chase on a searching Hassell-Collins kick had Gloucester scrambling back to defend their line before Wainwright scored his first try for the club.

Gloucester also had Freddie Thomas sin-binned for being offside, following repeat infringements from the visitors, but despite being a man down they managed to hit back through Trenholm, who crossed out wide after some bruising work from Morgan.

It took a try-saving tackle from Tom Whiteley on Will Joseph, and a follow-up effort from Tommy Reffell to knock the ball from the centre's grasp, to stop Gloucester from reducing the gap further.

A 50-22 kick from Searle after that had Tigers on their way to putting the game beyond doubt, as Hassell-Collins combined with Adam Radwan to finish on the left edge.

Still, Gloucester refused to leave the East Midlands empty handed, with Innard going over in the 79th minute for a bonus-point try which was then followed up with a Barton penalty that bagged the Cherry and Whites a losing bonus point as well.

'Five points and a big performance' - reaction

Leicester Tigers head coach Geoff Parling told BBC Radio Leicester:

"We have not started well in games repeatedly this season, and after 10 minutes it was a 14-0 lead [for Gloucester]. It felt like we hadn't thrown a punch, so I felt very calm there.

"And then there were some really, really good bits in the rest of the game.

"We actually feel a bit deflated because of the end of the game, giving them those two bonus points, but again that is a sign of the want and desire in the team. We got five points in a big performance against a team that has been going well."

Gloucester head coach George Skivington told BBC Radio Gloucestershire:

"It was a tough game. It was a very physical game, a lot of big collisions out there today.

"We are a little bit frustrated, I don't feel like we fired enough shots. Early on we got two opportunities and took them both and set ourselves up nicely. Then we weren't quite accurate enough, we probably lost too many balls in the air, dropped a few balls and you don't get many opportunities when you come to places like this and we let a few go in the first half.

"We didn't quite get a hold of it, but at the end I thought the bench came on and had a real impact and to come away with two points is something. But right now, I'd have liked the game to be 20 minutes longer."

articles.title: Glasgow Warriors 36-19 Connacht: Hosts secure bonus-point win in URC
articles.summary: Glasgow Warriors run in five tries to beat Connacht 36-19 and continue their unbeaten start to the United Rugby Championship season.
articles.body:
Tries : Hiddleston 2, Darge, McKay, Stephen Cons: Horne 4 Pens : Lancaster

Tries : Jansen, Ioane 2 Cons : Frawley 2

Glasgow Warriors ran in five tries against Connacht to claim a bonus-point win and continue their unbeaten start to the United Rugby Championship season.

After last weekend's draw with Ulster at Scotstoun, Warriors were gunning for their first home win of the campaign.

But it was Connacht who started on the front foot and number eight Sean Jansen found his way to the line to put the visitors in front.

The early stages were played almost exclusively in the home side's half, but on their first real foray into opposition territory Warriors sent a rolling line-out maul thundering over the Connacht line, with Gregor Hiddleston touching down.

The game was a little bitty, with neither side really getting their attacking game firing, so it was no surprise when Glasgow's second try came courtesy of another driving maul. Rory Darge was on hand to finish it off this time, and George Horne knocked over the conversion to put Warriors into a five-point lead.

The home side had exposed Connacht's weakness and were exploiting it ruthlessly. Prop Sam Illo was sent to the sin-bin for halting yet another rolling maul illegally as it headed for the visitors' line.

He need not have bothered as Glasgow simply kicked to the corner again, set the maul in motion and Hiddleston was left to touch down for his second try of the night to send them in at the break 12 points to the good.

If the first three Glasgow tries were all about power, the fourth was down to pure precision. Dan Lancaster found Jamie Dobie with a pinpoint cross-field kick and the wing gathered and cushioned a little grubber perfectly into the path of Josh McKay to go over for the bonus-point try.

Connacht were not quite done yet and Josh Ioane scored to give the visitors a little hope at 26-14.

That belief grew stronger when Ioane went over in the corner to make it a one-score game.

Connacht's momentum was checked when substitute Josh Murphy was sent to the sin-bin for a high shot on Seb Stephen and Glasgow punished them almost immediately with another rolling line-out maul, Stephen himself finishing it off to give Warriors some breathing space.

Lancaster popped over a straightforward penalty at the death as Glasgow sealed the maximum five points.

articles.title: Gallagher Prem: Aaron Wainwright scores his first try for Leicester Tigers as they defeat Gloucester in front of Prince Harry
articles.summary: Aaron Wainwright scores his first try for Leicester Tigers as they defeat Gloucester in high-scoring encounter at Mattioli Woods Welford Road Stadium; The Duke of Sussex, Prince Harry, was spotted in the stands
articles.body:
The hosts found themselves 14-0 down after just 10 minutes at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, but a sustained period of dominance led to them scoring 31 unanswered points that put them well on the way to their second straight win.

For the Cherry and Whites, this was a first league loss of the season as they fell short in a match that saw eight of the nine tries scored by forwards.

Prince Harry, who had a beer in his hand, is a keen rugby fan and was in attendance with Andrea Pinchen, the Tigers chief executive.

Harry returned to the UK with Meghan and their children in August after six years away in the US.

It was Leicester who quickly found themselves under pressure when they had fly-half Billy Searle sin-binned just three minutes in for deliberately knocking Ben Loader's pass forward inside his own 22.

The Cherry and Whites quickly made the most of their one-man advantage when Wales flanker Jac Morgan squeezed his way through after a succession of pick-and-goes from his fellow forwards.

Try number two for the visitors soon followed when a driving maul powered its way over, with loosehead Dian Bleuler grounding the ball. Caolan Englefield converted both early scores stylishly from out wide.

Shortly after Searle returned to the field, Leicester were on the board when Finn Carnduff managed to force himself over the whitewash from close quarters.

The Tigers began to dominate territorially and found themselves level after half an hour when England tighthead Joe Heyes blasted through from a couple of metres and Searle added the extras.

The turnaround was then completed in the 36th minute when Jamie Blamire scored off the back of a driving maul to give Leicester a 21-14 half-time lead.

The hosts then pulled away as Searle kicked a penalty before the bonus point was sealed in the 50th minute with yet another close-range effort as Wainwright this time crossed from a matter of inches.

To make matters worse for Gloucester, they had Thomas sin-binned immediately after the try had been awarded as their evening threatened to unravel.

They had a lifeline after an hour when a superb carry from Morgan took them close to the line before Englefield's pass allowed Will Trenholm to power in down the left.

But their hopes of a comeback were ended with 10 minutes remaining when Ollie Hassell-Collins became the first back from either team to score when Adam Radwan's pass sent him scurrying in at the corner.

There was still time, though, for the visitors to claim two bonus points late on as Jack Innard scored their fourth try before George Barton knocked over a penalty with the final kick.

articles.title: New Zealand v Australia: All Blacks power past Wallabies 50-19 to retain Bledisloe Cup
articles.summary: New Zealand retain the Bledisloe Cup for a 23rd straight year as they power past Australia to extend their remarkable unbeaten run at Eden Park.
articles.body:
Tries: Lakai, Vaai, Roigard, Taylor, Carter, Moorby, Jordan Cons: McKenzie (6) Pens: McKenzie

Tries: Wright, Wilson, Nasser Cons: Lonergan (2)

New Zealand retained the Bledisloe Cup for a 23rd straight year as they powered past Australia to extend their remarkable unbeaten run at Eden Park.

The All Blacks have not lost at the venue since 1994, with a dominant second-half display increasing their unbeaten run in Auckland to 54 Tests.

Australia remained in touch at half-time at 17-14 down but New Zealand blew the visitors away after the break, scoring five tries.

Peter Lakai, Tupou Vaa'i, Cam Roigard, Codie Taylor, Leroy Carter, Josh Moorby and Will Jordan all scored as fly-half Damian McKenzie kicked 15 points to help the All Blacks retain the trophy which is contested annually between the two nations.

Victory halted a three-match losing streak for the All Blacks after the 3-1 series defeat by world champions South Africa this summer.

Defeat for the Wallabies was their first since head coach Les Kiss succeeded Joe Schmidt in July, ending their six-game unbeaten run.

Australia were looking for their first win at Eden Park since 1986 and went ahead after controlling the early stages through full-back Tom Wright's try.

New Zealand responded strongly, and inspired by scrum-half Roigard's searching kicks, turned the match around with tries from Lakai and Vaa'i.

Wallabies captain Harry Wilson scored a try to keep New Zealand at arm's length, but the All Blacks moved through the gears in the second half.

Roigard grabbed a try for himself shortly after the break, before Taylor, Carter, Moorby and Jordan went over as Australia struggled to hold back the hosts' waves of attack.

Josh Nasser added a late try for the visitors, but the match was well beyond their reach by that point.

The second match of the two-Test series takes place in Sydney at the Accor Stadium on 17 October.

articles.title: New Zealand 50-19 Australia: All Blacks power to Eden Park victory to retain Bledisloe Cup for 24th year
articles.summary: Peter Lakai, Tupou Vaa'i, Cam Roigard, Codie Taylor, Leroy Carter, Josh Moorby, Will Jordan scores tries as All Blacks rip Australia apart in second half at Eden Park; Watch the All Blacks travel to face Australia in Sydney next Saturday October 17 (6am kick-off BST)
articles.body:
A competitive first half, perhaps even edged by Australia, saw the All Blacks three points ahead at the break as the sides traded two tries each. Back-rows Peter Lakai and Tupou Vaa'i scoring for the hosts, full-back Tom Wright and No 8 Harry Wilson scoring for the Wallabies.

But the second half proved altogether different, as the All Blacks added five further tries through scrum-half Cam Roigard, hooker Codie Taylor and wings Leroy Carter, Josh Moorby and Will Jordan.

Electric fly-half Damian McKenzie also added six conversions and a penalty in victory.

The success sees New Zealand remain unbeaten at Eden Park since 1994, and 2002 as the year Australia last held the Bledisloe Cup.

Australia, ​buoyed by a win over world champions South Africa last month, dominated the opening ⁠exchanges and got their reward in the eighth minute ⁠when full-back Wright cleverly straightened up an attacking move to score the opening try.

The aerial battle was always going to be a key factor and ‌New Zealand were enjoying the better of it with Jordie Barrett winning one duel and feeding McKenzie, who scythed through the defence before feeding flanker Lakai to level up the scores.

The All Blacks were also getting ‌a width in the attack that was causing Australia problems and the home side cashed in to take a 14-7 lead in the 16th minute, when Vaa'i barrelled low and hard through the defence at the end of a multi-phase attack.

Ryan Lonergan missed a penalty for Australia directly in front of the posts in the 24th minute, but McKenzie made ⁠no mistake nine minutes later to extend the lead to ​10 points.

The five minutes before half-time is traditionally a fruitful stage of ​the game for New Zealand, but it was Australia who scored three minutes before the ​break, with Ben Donaldson scooting through a gap in the defence and finding Wilson in support.

Australia ⁠again came firing out of the blocks in the second half but New Zealand earned the first points after 50 minutes when scrum-half Roigard darted over the line off the back of a rolling maul to extend their lead ⁠to 24-14.

The All Blacks were now relentless in attack ​and hooker Taylor, captaining the side for the second time, stepped to score their fourth try five minutes ​later.

The Wallabies were now struggling to hold onto the ball and wingers Carter, Moorby and Jordan capitalised on the remorseless pressure from the All Blacks in the ‌last quarter to put the game ​well beyond the visitors.

Barrett: It's special - the Bledisloe Cup means a lot to this country

All Blacks centre Jordie Barrett to Sky Sports:

"It's pretty special, the Bledisloe Cup means a lot to this country.

"We spent a lot of time on the road this year, and we spoke about it this week. We wanted to show what it was like to be an All Black and play in front of our fans.

"We're bloody proud of the performance tonight.

"We wanted to keep maxing out with our energy, and we got a lot of physical dominance up front tonight."

Wilson: We could tell New Zealand were hurting out there

Australia captain Harry Wilson to Sky Sports:

"Credit to New Zealand, they are a quality side, and playing them here [Eden Park] is always tough.

"We did a really good job to be in the fight after that first half, and then we had an opportunity at the start of the second half and blew it.

"It was then tough to get the ball back for the next 30 minutes.

"It was hard to hold your breath. They put us under a lot of pressure and you could tell they were hurting from the result of the South Africa series.

Next week sees the return clash between these two, as the All Blacks travel to face Australia in Sydney on Saturday October 17 (6am kick-off BST).

That match is also live on Sky Sports Main Event from 6am.

The Bledisloe Cup can now not be won by Australia, however, as even victory will see New Zealand retain it owing to Saturday's result.

articles.title: The Prem: Northampton 71-48 Bath: Saints score 11 tries to beat Bath in try-fest
articles.summary: Northampton win a high-octane 18-try thriller at home to Bath, the second highest-scoring game in English top-flight history.
articles.body:
Tries: F Smith, Sleightholme 3, Freeman 2, Dingwall, Pater, Kemeny, Mitchell, Coles Cons: F Smith 8

Tries: Carr-Smith, C Griffin, A Griffin, Green 2, Carreras, Bayliss Cons: Russell 5 Pens: Russell

Northampton came out on top of a high-octane 18-try thriller at home to Bath, the second highest scoring game in English top-flight history.

The two sides had surpassed 100 points on the scoreboard with 15 minutes remaining and continued to showcase unstoppable, attacking flair as the play went end-to-end.

Northampton eventually streaked clear in the second half, with Ollie Sleightholme scoring a hat-trick and Tommy Freeman scoring twice as they finished with 11 tries and bounced back from defeat by Bristol a week ago.

The loss is the first of the season for Bath, who made 12 changes for the match, with Arthur Green getting two of their seven tries and Charlie Griffin also scoring one on his Prem debut.

The 119 points scored falls short of the record in the English top flight - the 127 points shared in Saints' 94-33 win over Bristol in May.

Leicester battle back to beat Gloucester

Rory Hutchinson fed Fin Smith to cross first for Saints and while Bath arrived with a younger-looking starting XV there was no evidence of inexperience, as a moment of world-class Finn Russell skill opened a gap for Green to break through and Tom Carr-Smith to cross.

Bath hit Northampton again through 21-year-old Charlie Griffin before Saints slickly whipped the ball between their backs until it reached Sleightholme for their second try.

Tommy Freeman dived under the posts for Northampton's third right after Bath's Josh Bayliss was shown yellow for repeated infringements but, again, there was nothing to separate the sides as Archie Griffin rolled over under two tacklers for the visitors' third.

Kepu Tuipulotu barged through midfield and found Green to make it 26-19 to Bath, which was quickly cancelled out by Fraser Dingwall's score at the other end, leaving Russell's penalty on the stroke of half-time the only mark of difference.

Green doubled his tally quickly after the restart, but Saints full-back James Pater pounced on Santiago Carreras' dropped ball to steal possession and sprint the distance to the line.

Carreras made amends with a try of his own although Northampton started turning the screw despite Bath unloading their bench of big-hitters.

Josh Kemeny scored in the corner, Alex Mitchell followed - collecting his own grubber kick in a solo showpiece - and Sleightholme capped a superb move that saw Saints turn the ball over by their own line and sweep up the field.

Sleightholme completed his hat-trick four minutes later and while Bayliss kept Bath in touch to close the gap to 57-48, it did not last as Saints had more in the tank.

Alex Coles barged over before Freeman rounded off a blockbuster day in the closing stages.

'We don't want it to be basketball' - reaction

Northampton Saints head coach Sam Vesty told BBC Radio Northampton:

"Both teams took opportunities pretty quickly and I think both teams will be slightly disappointed in how they exited their end, in terms of when they've got the ball and got control of it.

"We gave it up quite a lot to them and put ourselves defensively under pressure We're not happy with the 48 part of that scoreline.

"We don't want it to be basketball. Obviously lots and lots of very good stuff but there's a good couple of areas for us to focus to be better - a more ruthless Bath and that's a very different game.

[On the attack] "We were so clinical with our execution of what we were doing. Absolutely fantastic.

"I thought our breakdown was very good, lots and lots of positives but we need to be better coming out of our end."

Bath head of rugby Johann van Graan told BBC Radio Bristol:

"It's dsappointing if you score 48 points away from home and lose the game.

"I think we lost control between minutes 50 and 60. The back end of both halves we conceded a yellow card and against a team like Saints it's difficult to contain them.

"But look at the positives, we played some fantastic rugby today."

articles.title: Edinburgh top URC after bonus-point win over Zebre
articles.summary: Edinburgh go top of the nascent United Rugby Championship table as a bonus-point victory at Zebre makes it three wins from three.
articles.body:
Tries: M. Currie, Douglas, Bradbury, T. Currie Cons: Grayson 3 Pens: Grayson

Edinburgh went top of the nascent United Rugby Championship table as a bonus-point victory at Zebre made it three wins from three for Sean Everitt's injury-hit side.

James Grayson kicked a penalty to put the visitors in front early on, but after winger Malelili Satala was sin-binned for a deliberate knock-on, Italy scrum-half Alessandro Fusco put Zebre in front with the game's first try.

Edinburgh recovered from that setback though and retook the lead on the half-hour mark when centre Matt Currie crashed through a couple of Zebre defenders to dot down.

From that moment, Edinburgh never ceded control.

With half-time approaching, Fusco was yellow carded and from the subsequent attack, young flanker Freddy Douglas scored at the back of an Edinburgh maul.

The game followed a similar pattern after the break, with the Scottish outfit dominating both possession and territory.

Magnus Bradbury powered over under the posts for Edinburgh's third try and although Zebre's Giacamo Ferrari narrowed the deficit after Edinburgh's replacement hooker Harri Morris was yellow carded, the hosts never threatened to turn things around.

And in the final minute of the contest, another powerful maul allowed Tom Currie to score Edinburgh's fourth try and ensure they would take maximum points.

articles.title: Gallagher Prem: Northampton Saints run riot to defeat Bath 71-48 in second highest-scoring game in history of competition
articles.summary: Ollie Sleightholme scores a hat-trick as Gallagher Prem champions Northampton Saints thump Bath 71-48 on an astonishing afternoon at DPD Stadium at Franklin's Gardens
articles.body:
Eighteen tries were scored in total, with Saints bouncing back from defeat at Bristol Bears last week in spectacular style.

Ollie Sleightholme scored a hat-trick in an astonishing afternoon at Franklin's Gardens in which 119 points were scored.

"We put our game on the pitch," Sleightholme said on TNT Sports . "We don't want to concede that many points, so we've got stuff to work on.

"It's wicked [to play in this team]. We know we're going to create opportunities. We capitalised on the ones that we got.

"It was very loud. I haven't heard it like this for a while. It's great to be back."

Saints are also at the centre of the highest-scoring game in Prem history when they scored 14 tries to humiliate Bristol Bears 94-33 at Franklin's Gardens in May .

The total of 127 points meant it was the highest-scoring game in the history of English top-flight rugby union, beating the previous record of 118 in Richmond's 106-12 win over Bedford in 1999.

Northampton struck first after seven minutes when Fin Smith glided through a gap for the opener, which he could not convert.

Bath's response was excellent and swift as Finn Russell's off-load sent Arthur Green into space, with his pass inside giving Tom Carr-Smith an easy finish and Russell a simple conversion.

The visitors were over again three minutes later following a tapped penalty as Carr-Smith whipped a pass left for Charlie Griffin to finish in the corner, with Russell converting brilliantly.

The Saints were quickly back in business, though, as some wonderful quick hands led to Tommy Freeman off-loading to James Pater, whose long pass put Sleightholme in the clear, Smith's conversion making it a two-point game.

After Bath had Josh Bayliss sin-binned for killing the ball close to his own line, Northampton took the lead when Smith's pass put Freeman under the posts.

Despite being down to 14 men, Bath hit back hard again as they levelled at 19-19 when tighthead Archie Griffin barged his way over from close range down the right.

And they led when Kepu Tuipulotu broke through some flimsy tackling before putting Green in the clear, although Saints soon squared proceedings once more when their captain, Fraser Dingwall, glided through.

Russell's penalty with the final kick of a breathless first half had Bath 29-26 ahead at the break, and they extended their lead within two minutes of the restart when Carr-Smith set up Green's second of the afternoon.

Saints were momentarily back within three points when Pater ran in after Santi Carreras fumbled Russell's pass, but the Argentinian soon made amends when Russell's looping ball gave him a walk-in.

Back came Northampton again when Josh Kemeny scored in the corner from Alex Coles' pass to make it a dozen tries shared between the two teams in 51 minutes.

And Saints led again when Alex Mitchell scored a lovely individual try by collecting his own kick ahead before Sleightholme's second score brought up 50 points for the hosts.

There was just no let-up as Sleightholme ran in under the posts to complete his hat-trick, with Bayliss pulling a score back for Bath before Smith's strong carry allowed Coles to get in on the act.

There was time for one more try as more quick hands from Rory Hutchinson and Anthony Belleau put Freeman in for his second, and Northampton's 11th, of an extraordinary afternoon.

Dowson: High-scoring clash due to 'different mindset'

Saints director of rugby Phil Dowson thinks high-scoring matches is due to teams shifting in mindset in recent years.

Dowson said: "There have been some rule changes from a kicking point of view that's opened the game up and the best ball to play off is broken field, counter-attack turnover ball. You get a lot more of that.

"I think the ability of teams now - all teams - have an appetite to move the ball on the counter attack first before kicking first, so I think there's a different mindset.

"I think risk is being rewarded more often and there's the actual skill level of the playing group.

"You can talk about the underfoot conditions, the way it's being refereed, all that sort of stuff, you're still seeing tons of turnover at the breakdown.

"We don't want it to be 99-88 - not basketball, and I hear that in the media from some coaches - but we also don't want 9-3, so we've got to find a balance in how we run the game.

"But at the moment there are lots of Saints fans happy."

Bristol have now failed to win in all eight of their Prem visits to Saracens' home since they reached the top flight, with this loss also their first defeat of the 2026-27 campaign.

Saracens' star wing Noah Caluori dived into the corner to touch down one-handed immediately into his first Prem start of the season, and Owen Farrell kicked two penalties to make it 11-0 to the hosts at the break.

While Harry Randall put Bristol on the board early in the second half, tries from Alex O'Driscoll and Jack Bracken, plus a penalty try, ensured Saracens took the maximum five points from the match.

articles.title: Ulster 26-26 Munster: Ulster fight back to earn thrilling URC draw in Belfast
articles.summary: A second-half fightback earns Ulster a draw against Munster in a thrilling United Rugby Championship Irish derby in Belfast.
articles.body:
Tries: Stockdale 2, McCann, McCloskey Cons: Murphy 3

Tries: Kendellen 2, Van der Merwe, Kelly Cons: Hanrahan 3

A second-half fightback earned Ulster a draw against Munster in a thrilling United Rugby Championship Irish derby in Belfast.

Munster looked on course for a bonus-point win after first-half tries from Alex Kendellen (2), Marnus van der Merwe and Dan Kelly put them 26-5 up at the break.

However, having already marked his 150th appearance with a superb solo try in the first half, Jacob Stockdale's second raised Ulster's hopes of a turnaround.

David McCann further cut the gap, and after replacement Munster fly-half Charlie O'Shea kicked a penalty short, Stuart McCloskey touched down three minutes from time to ensure a share of the spoils.

It is a second successive draw for Ulster after last week's 33-33 tie with Glasgow, although an opening loss to Edinburgh leaves Richie Murphy's team still searching for their first win of the season.

Ulster playing games like training sessions - Murphy

Edinburgh top URC after bonus-point win over Zebre

Leinster stroll past Cardiff for happy homecoming

After Munster head coach Clayton McMillan admitted midweek that last season's dismal 28-3 loss in Belfast remains "etched" in his memory, it was perhaps unsurprising to see his side fired up for the season's first interpro.

They were helped by Ulster, though, who looked sluggish and ill-disciplined early on, having also been slow out of the blocks at home to Edinburgh a fortnight ago.

Ulster's early handling errors handed Munster chances to strike and they took the lead when Kendellen crashed down following a maul.

That try jolted Ulster into life, and after a scrum on the edge of the Munster 22, Ethan McIlroy fed Stockdale, who barged past two red shirts to score a fine try, which stood following a lengthy television match official (TMO) check to see if Stuart McCloskey had tripped Shay McCarthy.

However, Stockdale's surge of inspiration proved a fleeting moment of joy for the hosts as Munster reasserted control through their pack, who constructed another effective maul for Van der Merwe to score.

Matters only got worse for Ulster. Having already lost second row Eli Snyman to a head knock, Cormac Izuchukwu was yellow carded after his shoulder struck Gavin Coombes' head at a ruck.

Within a couple of minutes of Izuchukwu's exit, Hanrahan sent Kelly through a gap in the Ulster defence to extend Munster's lead.

Then, with Ireland head coach Andy Farrell watching from the stands, Kendellen crossed for the second time to seal the away side's bonus point before half time and deepen the hosts' malaise.

Murphy's response to his side's struggles was to introduce Tom McAllister and James McNabney at the break, closely followed by Tom O'Toole and Matthew Devine.

O'Toole - on his first appearance of the season - looked especially sharp and it was his surge forward that created the opening for Rob Baloucoune to sprint towards the line and tee up Stockdale.

McCann then scored following a period of sustained pressure to bring Ulster to within a score before O'Shea kicked his penalty short, having had to scramble after the ball fell off the tee.

With time running out, Ulster pushed for the equalising score and McCloskey - on his first outing this season after an outstanding 2025-26 campaign - barged his way over before Jack Murphy held his nerve to send his conversion between the posts and level the match.

Ulster travel to Zebre for the start of their Challenge Cup campaign on 17 October (15:15 BST) while Munster host Racing in the Champions Cup later that day (20:00)

articles.title: Leinster 29-5 Cardiff: Irish province win on URC return to Laya Arena
articles.summary: Champions Leinster score five tries to beat Cardiff in Dublin for their first win of the 2026-27 United Rugby Championship campaign.
articles.body:
Tries: Keenan, J O'Brien 2, Conan, Osborne Cons: Prendergast 2

Champions Leinster made a successful return to the revamped Laya Arena by beating Cardiff in the United Rugby Championship (URC).

The Irish province recorded their first victory of the 2026-27 season in front of 20,600 supporters, and condemned the Blue and Blacks to a first loss.

Leinster scored three tries inside the first quarter through Hugo Keenan, Jimmy O'Brien and Jack Conan, then O'Brien's second in the 37th minute secured the four-try bonus.

But, with a raft of Ireland internationals making their first outings of the campaign, the second half was flat and scoreless until Jamie Osborne went over with five minutes to go.

Cardiff failed to claim a URC match point just once when making the play-offs last season, but left Dublin without anything after being limited to Mason Grady's first-half try.

Ulster fight back to draw with Munster in thriller

Costelow kick seals Scarlets' first league win

Leo Cullen's side started the defence of their title in South Africa and returned with three bonus points from defeats by Lions and Sharks.

The head coach brought back his big hitters to ensure it was a successful return to the redeveloped €52m Laya Arena, formerly the RDS Arena, after two seasons playing at Aviva Stadium.

A sell-out crowd was treated to a glitzy pre-match show and then a rapid Leinster start, with the hosts hitting the front when full-back Keenan kicked ahead and gathered after being found on the left wing by fast handling.

Cardiff scrum-half Aled Davies was sin-binned for cynically killing the ball on his line and tries followed by wing O'Brien and number eight Conan.

It looked set to be a long night for the Welsh side but they made light of being a man down to make it 15-5 thanks to the cunning of Callum Sheedy.

The Wales fly-half caught Leinster sleeping from a penalty to find Grady on the wing with a cross-kick.

But the hosts were in control at half-time thanks to a set play that foxed Cardiff to give O'Brien a run-in for a fourth try down the same flank, Sam Prendergast kicking his first conversion for a 22-5 lead.

Cardiff lacked the power - or accuracy - to make a dent in the Leinster defence from several entries into the 22 after the restart.

The Welsh side had plenty of territory and showed tenacity in a subdued atmosphere, but it was centre Osborne that got the first score of the half in the closing stages with a strong finish from close range.

Cardiff named eight Taulupe Faletau in their starting line-up on Thursday afternoon, although boss Corniel van Zyl admitted the Wales number eight still had a few boxes to tick because of niggles.

The Blue and Blacks opted against fielding the 35-year-old for the first time since a shoulder injury suffered at Sharks in March.

In-form Taine Basham was a late inclusion and continued his strong start to the season as his side's most dynamic carrier.

Cardiff travel to free-flowing Northampton in the Champions Cup on Sunday, 18 October (17:30 BST).

With a five-day turnaround from that fixture to a home URC game against Sharks, they must choose the right time to reintegrate Faletau.

articles.title: Ulster 26-26 Munster: Richie Murphy says Ulster are 'playing matches like they're training sessions'
articles.summary: Head coach Richie Murphy says UIster are "playing matches like training sessions" as he expresses his disappointment after Saturday's 26-26 draw with Munster in Belfast.
articles.body:
Head coach Richie Murphy says UIster are "playing matches like they're training sessions" as he expressed his disappointment with his side's slow start in Saturday's 26-26 draw with Munster in Belfast.

Trailing by 21 points at the break, Ulster hit back as Jacob Stockdale scored his second try of the game before David McCann and Stuart McCloskey struck to earn a second successive United Rugby Championship draw.

Having opened the campaign with a home defeat by Edinburgh and a 33-33 draw in Glasgow, Murphy's side remain winless on the domestic front before starting their European campaign next week.

"We're still very much in the early part of the season. We've got three our four players coming back in for their first games this weekend," said Murphy.

"The flow of the team hasn't completely settled in. At the moment, we're playing matches like they're training sessions.

"We're overplaying with the ball in the middle of the park, we need to start applying more pressure to the opposition.

"That's going to be a key part that we need to learn from this week."

Despite the return of Ireland internationals Stockdale, McCloskey and Nick Timoney, Ulster struggled against a powerful display from Munster in the first half as tries from Alex Kendellen (2), Marnus van der Merwe and Dan Kelly put Clayton McMillan's side in the driving seat at the break.

But despite a spirited second-half showing to earn another three points after last week's draw in Glasgow, Murphy said he was "bitterly disappointed" when asked if he was left with mixed emotions.

"We allowed Munster to set the tempo, we were inaccurate with our first launch, so that we kicked off, they kicked out, so we were inaccurate with that first launch," added Murphy.

"Off the back of that, penalty, penalty and then you're back in your corner and fighting for your life.

"Once you're five metres out and the opposition have a line-out, it's very hard to stop, so that gave them control of the first half."

Having pegged Munster back, Ulster could have won the game with the final play, but Robert Baloucoune's attempted pass to Matthew Devine was cut out by Alex Nankivell as the hosts' winless URC run stretched to seven games.

"Coming in at half-time, I thought the lads reacted really well," added Murphy.

"We made some changes, still very inaccurate in the second half and didn't look after the ball well enough, didn't control field position at all in the game, but ultimately we got into a situation where last play of the game we were running at them and gave them the ball back again.

"Our turnover rate needs to come down, our scrum has been going really well but took a backward step tonight and I kind of feel like we didn't attack the game the way we needed to."

Munster boss McMillan was similarly downbeat after his side were held scoreless in the second half to let slip a 21-point advantage.

"We talked about it at half-time that Ulster are a quality side that won't go away," he said.

"We needed to continue to be accurate and just apply pressure in the right parts of the field.

"But we didn't quite get the same quality of possession in the second half, and Ulster were good enough to find a way back into the game."
